section: Adjoining end side panel for N_Elle with framed door
source_pages: printed p.446-447 / PDF 448-449, both pages read whole 2026-08-26
extraction_note: The third collection of the same article. Taken on 2026-08-26 with the other two. RELEVANT BEYOND THE COLLECTION QUESTION: on 2026-08-26 Andriy asked that the filler beside the west glass row be ordered in the colour of the GLASS DOOR'S FRAME (see fillers_wall_h96.json). A framed door is what this page is for, and its band set says so.
band_note: BANDS 12, 13 AND 15 - not 1 to 11. The framed-door collection is priced on its own band set, exactly as the N_Elle framed filler is on printed p.435 (YC0150, bands 12/13/15). Band 15 is '-' on every panel row.
depth_note: EVERY GROUP PRINTS TWO NUMBERS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER. The label names the CARCASS depth the panel serves ('for 35-cm deep side panel + door thickness'); the 'd.' beside it is the depth the catalog DRAWS. Across all eight groups in this chapter the second is the first plus 2,2 per door face, rounded up - 35 -> 37,2 -> d.37,5; 70 -> 74,4 -> d.75; 124 -> 128,4 -> d.129. That arithmetic is DERIVED and is written here to explain the numbers, not to replace them: depth_mm below is the printed 'd.' verbatim. Whether 'd.' describes the finished end or the panel's own board is Elda Q21, and everything drawn at the end of a run depends on the answer.
label_collision_note: TWO GROUPS ON THIS PAGE CARRY THE SAME PRINTED LABEL. Both the d.102 and the d.107 group are printed 'for 62+35-cm deep side panel'. They cannot both be. The codes disagree with the label: at the heights where the letters are unambiguous the d.102 rows carry the prefixes this same chapter uses for a 62-deep panel and the d.107 rows carry the 67-deep prefixes, and the arithmetic in depth_note gives 62+35 -> 101,4 -> d.102 and 67+35 -> 106,4 -> d.107. The label is kept verbatim in printed_depth_label; the reading is Elda Q20. NOTE the letters are only a witness at the SHORT heights - from H.138 up, both groups use F-prefixes and are told apart by the trailing digits alone, which is domain rule 5 restated: a code is a lookup, never a decode.
surcharge_note: Printed beside these tables and NOT on any other collection's: 'Adjoined end side panel with 45 degree lip in NATURAL STONE and ENGINEERED STONE finishes' - 84 points 1 side, 168 points 2 sides; 'Adjoined end side panel with 45 degree lip in CERAMIC finishes' - 134 points 1 side, 267 points 2 sides, and 'The ceramic end panel is supplied with an aluminium frame'. The opposite-hinge page adds: 'For Natural Stone and Engineered Stone on P. 129, please contact Cesar for costs and feasibility' - i.e. the deepest back-to-back group has no printed price in stone at all.

end_panel_45.description: Adjoining end side panel for N_Elle with framed door, 2.2 cm thick - with 45 degree vertical edge
end_panel_45.handed_note: The ARTICLE has no hand. A panel does not open, so there is no hinge to hand, and the catalog prints one code for either end of a run. What IS handed is the 45-degree edge, which must face the door - and that follows from which end you place it at, so it is placement and not an attribute. The choice the catalog DOES price is a different one: which page you are on. See the two unit types in this file.

front_layout.note: A PANEL HAS NO FRONT. 'none' is stated rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs defaults a missing layout to 'single' and would hang a door leaf on a flat board. A default is not a source.

page_split_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-26, SAME EVENING, AND THE ORIGINAL CLAIM IS LEFT BELOW SO THE MISTAKE IS READABLE. The note said: 'THIS IS A DIFFERENT ARTICLE, NOT A VARIANT. The two pages price the same heights and the same depth groups under different codes.' THAT IS FALSE, and one lookup against the real kitchen showed it. The two pages of a collection price DISJOINT depth groups - there is no height-and-depth that appears on both, so no comparison between them is possible and nothing was ever mirrored. What is worse for the reading I gave: WHICH page a group falls on CHANGES BY COLLECTION. Maxima puts 35+35 on the banner page (printed p.441); N_Elle puts 35+35 on the 45-degree page (printed p.444) and starts its banner page at 62+35. So the banner does not partition single from back-to-back either. WHAT IS CERTAIN: each code came from one printed page, and the two type keys record which. WHAT THE BANNER MEANS - whether p.441 is a different article for the same situation, or the same table continuing across a spread with a note that applies to its own rows - IS NOT DECIDABLE FROM THE PAGES. The drawings on the two pages are the same drawing. Elda Q22. Until it is answered the depth group decides the code and the page choice decides nothing, because the groups do not overlap.
